title: Study of a VTOL air vehicle based on ducted contra-rotating propellers.
author: Marcelo Romano Berger
abstract: This is a final year project in Aeronautics Engineering from the Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica. It was undertaken in the propulsion laboratory of the host institution of SUPAERO, Toulouse, France. It was developed under the guidance of M. Roger Barčnes, at SUPAERO and M. Amílcar Porto Pimenta at ITA. It studies the forces and moments generated by a vertical take off and landing (VTOL) mini air vehicle (MAV) and analyze also the flight qualities of the system through a model built in the software SIMULINK. The report begins with an introduction, which summarizes the motivation of the studies, the MAV's applications and the advantages of using a system propelled by ducted contra-rotating propellers. In a first moment, the validation of a test bench to measure the forces and moments generated by the vehicle is also described. It concludes that the test bench is able to give reasonable results, but rigid systems must be used with it. After that, the report the theory behind the propulsion of the MAV is summarized. It is followed by the developing of a flight mechanics model, which is used in a SIMULINK program in order to better understand the vehicle flight qualities. The results acquired in the test bench and the flight simulations of the drone are given in the following chapters. Finally, important conclusions and comments about those results are exposed. There are two main conclusions. The first one is that propulsion system and control surfaces of the vehicle are able to generate enough efforts to a controlled flight. The second one is that the different positions of the gravity center change considerably the behavior of the system. The choice of the system configuration must be made than according to the desired flight characteristics: stability and/or maneuverability.
subjects: Aeronaves de decolagem vertical e curta
